# T2 round 3: Watcher-like severity tiers (generated by tracks/r3_t2/make_report.py)

> Annotated copy of results/r3_t2/tables.md (audit issue m11; generated by tracks/fixes/e5/m11_annotate_r3t2.py). Numbers are unchanged; caveats were added to the sections that contain akshn_adj rows.

## Severity-tier composition of traffic

> **Label-leakage caveat (akshn_adj rows).** The akshn_adj severity is aksh-n's outcome-adjudicated `overall_severity`, assigned with knowledge of whether the trajectory is an attack (honest runs 97% tier 1-3, attacks 87% tier >= 7; severity AUROC 0.998). It is not something a deployed rater can see. Every akshn_adj result that uses severity (watcher_perm / watcher_strict, tier_w / tier_opt, sev_tilt, stack_sev, mm_cell_sev, tilt_mm, and the severity-tier composition) is a label-leaking upper bound, not an achievable operating point. The blind severity rater used for the mb_* panels (no side task, no reasoning) gives severity AUROC 0.53-0.54. The suspicion-only rules on akshn_adj (global, cfar, stack) do not use severity for thresholding but are evaluated with the adjudicated damage weights.

Share of actions per Watcher tier (1-3 / 4-6 / 7-8 / 9-10), share of trajectories containing at least one action of the tier, mean attack damage, and trajectory-level AUROC of suspicion (max) and of severity (max) for attack vs honest.

## Policy comparison (spend-matched)

> **Label-leakage caveat (akshn_adj rows).** The akshn_adj severity is aksh-n's outcome-adjudicated `overall_severity`, assigned with knowledge of whether the trajectory is an attack (honest runs 97% tier 1-3, attacks 87% tier >= 7; severity AUROC 0.998). It is not something a deployed rater can see. Every akshn_adj result that uses severity (watcher_perm / watcher_strict, tier_w / tier_opt, sev_tilt, stack_sev, mm_cell_sev, tilt_mm, and the severity-tier composition) is a label-leaking upper bound, not an achievable operating point. The blind severity rater used for the mb_* panels (no side task, no reasoning) gives severity AUROC 0.53-0.54. The suspicion-only rules on akshn_adj (global, cfar, stack) do not use severity for thresholding but are evaluated with the adjudicated damage weights.

`dmg_unif` = damage-weighted detection vs a uniform attacker; `dmg_org` = 1 − expected undetected damage / 10 in the org an informed attacker picks; `dmg_cell` = same when the attacker picks an (org, damage tier) cell (severity-aware attacker); Δ = paired bootstrap difference vs global. `feasible` = share of replicates where the policy can spend exactly B (tier gating can cap the reachable spend, the always-block tier can exceed it); `matched_ok` = B inside the swept range.

## Nominal-mode realized spend (B = 1% and 5%)

> **Label-leakage caveat (akshn_adj rows).** The akshn_adj severity is aksh-n's outcome-adjudicated `overall_severity`, assigned with knowledge of whether the trajectory is an attack (honest runs 97% tier 1-3, attacks 87% tier >= 7; severity AUROC 0.998). It is not something a deployed rater can see. Every akshn_adj result that uses severity (watcher_perm / watcher_strict, tier_w / tier_opt, sev_tilt, stack_sev, mm_cell_sev, tilt_mm, and the severity-tier composition) is a label-leaking upper bound, not an achievable operating point. The blind severity rater used for the mb_* panels (no side task, no reasoning) gives severity AUROC 0.53-0.54. The suspicion-only rules on akshn_adj (global, cfar, stack) do not use severity for thresholding but are evaluated with the adjudicated damage weights.
